keyTakeaways: From 1 April 2026, an employer's gifts, vouchers and tokens are valued at nil only below ₹15,000 in aggregate per tax year (Rule 15, Income-tax Rules, 2026); the old line was ₹5,000.
A CBIC press release of 10 July 2017 puts employer gifts of up to ₹50,000 a year per employee outside GST.
In a workplace field experiment, a €7 thermos raised output about 25% while €7 in cash raised it about 5%, and offering a choice kept the 25% even though 18 of 22 workers chose cash.
Festival thanks get left late: 49.4% of SubhSandesh's Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages were built on the day itself (n = 89, a different festival), so order physical gifts weeks ahead.

faqs.question: Is a Diwali gift from my employer taxable in India?
faqs.answer: Only if your gifts, vouchers and tokens from the employer reach ₹15,000 in the tax year. Rule 15 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026 values them at nil below that line, counting gifts to your household too. Your employer's payroll team applies it, so check with your CA if you received several gifts in one year.

faqs.question: Did the tax-free limit on employer gifts change in 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Income-tax Rules, 2026 came into force on 1 April 2026 and set the line at ₹15,000 in aggregate per tax year. Under the 1962 Rules it was ₹5,000, so a gift given in March 2026 fell under the old figure.

faqs.question: Does a Diwali gift voucher count toward the ₹15,000?
faqs.answer: Yes. The rule names a gift, voucher or token in lieu of a gift, so an e-voucher or gift card counts the same as a hamper. Add every voucher the employee receives in the tax year, not just the Diwali one.

faqs.question: Is a cash Diwali bonus treated the same as a gift?
faqs.answer: Cash is not named in the rule's wording, which speaks of a gift, voucher or token. A cash payment normally runs through payroll as salary, so do not assume the ₹15,000 treatment applies to it; ask your CA before you label cash as a gift.

faqs.question: Does GST apply when a company gives Diwali gifts to staff?
faqs.answer: A CBIC press release of 10 July 2017 says employer gifts up to ₹50,000 a year per employee are outside GST. Gifts above that, given without consideration in the course of business, are taxable. Input tax credit on the purchase is a separate question for your CA.

faqs.question: How much should a company spend per employee on Diwali gifts?
faqs.answer: Most teams can work in the ₹500–2,500 band (EST, Oct 2026), which uses 4–17% of the yearly ₹15,000 line and leaves room for birthdays and awards. Larger amounts suit long-service milestones or very small teams. Set the yearly total first, then the Diwali share.

faqs.question: What can I give employees for Diwali under ₹1,000?
faqs.answer: One daily-use item such as an insulated steel bottle, a steel lunch box or a small brass diya pair, at about ₹600–1,000 (EST, Oct 2026). For large teams, a 250–500 g box of one regional sweet from a local shop costs about ₹250–450.

faqs.question: Should every employee get the same Diwali gift?
faqs.answer: Same value, not necessarily the same item. In Kube, Maréchal and Puppe's experiment, workers offered a choice of cash or a gift worked about 25% harder than the baseline even though 18 of 22 picked cash, so a three-item choice form at one price is worth the extra step.

faqs.question: When should we order Diwali gifts for Diwali 2027?
faqs.answer: Diwali 2027 falls on Friday 29 October, with Dhanteras on 27 October. Our planning estimate is 2–4 weeks for bulk stock and a choice form, so place orders by the start of October 2027. Write the personal notes early too.

faqs.question: Can I send my whole team a Diwali card through SubhSandesh?
faqs.answer: Not as a team broadcast. SubhSandesh's Diwali page is built for one recipient, in love, family or friend mode, and takes about five minutes. Use it for one colleague who is also a close friend, and use your HR channel for the team greeting.

faqs.question: Do employees prefer cash or a gift?
faqs.answer: When asked, most choose cash: 18 of 22 workers did in a 2010 workplace field experiment. Yet a €7 thermos raised output about 25% against about 5% for €7 in cash, so stated preference and effect point in different directions.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Diwali Gift Ideas for Employees, by Budget and Tax Year

The simplest of all Diwali gift ideas for employees is one useful thing in a fixed band, usually ₹500–2,500 a head (EST, Oct 2026), with a signed note, and a plan that keeps each person's gifts for the whole tax year below ₹15,000. That ₹15,000 line is new: Rule 15 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, in force from 1 April 2026, values employer gifts at nil only below it, where the old limit was ₹5,000. Order early, because people leave festival thanks late: on SubhSandesh, 49.4% of Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages were built on the festival day itself, and 48.3% of all shared pages are opened on a phone. Those are Raksha Bandhan and platform figures, not Diwali or corporate data, and the Raksha Bandhan sample is only 89 pages.

Below: the tax and GST lines with their sources, five budget bands, what two workplace experiments found, a comparison table, and where this approach goes wrong. None of it is tax advice; check with your CA before you run it through payroll.

## What counts as an employee Diwali gift under Indian tax rules in 2026?

An employee Diwali gift, for tax purposes, is a gift, voucher or token given by the employer to an employee or a member of their household, on a ceremonial occasion or otherwise. Indian tax law treats it as a perquisite, part of salary, unless its value stays under a yearly threshold.

The threshold moved this year. The [Income-tax Rules, 2026, notified on 20 March 2026](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/en-notified-it-rules-2026-20-03-2026-pdf), came into force on 1 April 2026, and row 4 of the table in Rule 15 says the value is nil "if the value of such gift, voucher or token, as the case may be, is below ₹15,000 in aggregate during the tax year". Under the 1962 Rules, the Income Tax Department's [perquisites summary](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/perquisites) put the same line at ₹5,000.

GST is a separate test with a separate number. A [CBIC press release of 10 July 2017](https://cbic-gst.gov.in/pdf/press-release/pres-rls-gst-gift-dt10july.pdf) says gifts up to ₹50,000 a year from an employer to an employee are outside GST, and that gifts above it, made without consideration, are taxable when made in the course or furtherance of business.

## How the ₹15,000 line works across a whole year of gifts

The rule counts every gift, voucher and token in the tax year, not one festival. Diwali 2027 falls on Friday 29 October 2027, inside tax year 2027–28, so it shares the line with that year's birthday vouchers, Holi sweets and work-anniversary awards.

A typical mid-size plan stays well clear. A ₹2,000 Diwali hamper, a ₹1,000 birthday voucher, ₹500 of Holi mithai and a ₹3,000 long-service award add up to ₹6,500 per person.

A single expensive Diwali gift is where it goes wrong. A ₹12,000 phone plus a ₹3,000 New Year voucher reaches ₹15,000, which is not below the line; read literally, the rule then values the gift at its full amount, not just the excess. That reading is ours, from the rule's text, so put the specific case to your CA.

## Diwali gift ideas for employees in five budget bands

Each band below gives the same four things: what to give, who it suits, the estimated price per head, and how much of the yearly ₹15,000 it uses. Prices are our estimates for October 2026, not quotes, and bulk rates vary.

### 1. Under ₹500: a regional sweet from a local mithai shop

Give 250–500 g of one good regional sweet from a shop near the office, rather than a mixed box. It suits large teams, interns and contract-heavy sites where the headcount runs into hundreds. Expect about ₹250–450 per box (EST, Oct 2026). It uses roughly 2–3% of the yearly ₹15,000, which leaves room for every other occasion.

### 2. ₹500–1,000: one daily-use item, chosen once

An insulated steel bottle, a steel lunch box or a small brass diya pair works because it gets used, and nobody has to store it. It suits teams of 50–500 where you cannot learn individual tastes. Expect about ₹600–1,000 (EST, Oct 2026). It uses 4–7% of the line, and it is the band most "under ₹1,000" searches are really asking about.

### 3. ₹1,000–2,500: a choice of three

Pick three items at the same price, say a dry-fruit tin, a desk plant and a power bank, and let each person choose by form. It suits teams up to about 100, where a form is easy to run. Expect about ₹1,200–2,500 (EST, Oct 2026). It uses 8–17% of the line; the next section explains why offering the choice matters.

### 4. ₹2,500–5,000: something for the home

A pressure cooker, a mixer-grinder or a brass puja thali set lands with the employee's household, which the rule explicitly includes. It suits smaller firms and teams whose families come to the Diwali party. Expect about ₹2,800–5,000 (EST, Oct 2026). It uses 19–33% of the line, so check what else the year holds.

### 5. Above ₹5,000: long service or a small founding team

Wireless earbuds, a smartwatch or a weekend stay voucher signals more than thanks, so keep it for five-year milestones or a team of under ten. Expect about ₹5,000–10,000 (EST, Oct 2026). It uses a third to two-thirds of the line in one go, which is exactly where the year's total needs a spreadsheet and your CA.

## What employees respond to, according to two workplace experiments

The gift itself can beat the same amount in cash. In a field experiment by [Kube, Maréchal and Puppe (KIT working paper, April 2011)](https://econpapers.wiwi.kit.edu/downloads/KITe_WP_25.pdf), temporary data-entry workers given an unexpected €7 thermos bottle entered about 25% more characters than a baseline group, while a €7 cash raise moved output about 5%. The same €7 in cash folded into an origami shirt produced a 29.3% gain.

What people say they want is a different question. When 22 workers were offered the cash or the bottle, 18 took the cash, yet that group's output still rose about 25%, as much as the bottle group's. Offering a choice carried the effect, which is the case for the band 3 form.

Recognition without money also moved effort. In a [ZEW field experiment from March 2013](https://www.zew.de/fileadmin/FTP/dp/dp13017.pdf), 363 people hired for a three-hour data-entry job were randomly handed thank-you cards after two hours, and subsequent performance rose substantially, most of all when cards went only to the best performers. Both studies are short, one-off data-entry jobs paid in euros, not salaried staff in India, so treat them as direction, not a forecast.

## Five budget bands compared

The table puts each band's estimated price next to its share of the yearly ₹15,000 and the planning time it needs.

| Band | EST price per head (Oct 2026) | Share of ₹15,000 tax-year line | Planning time (our estimate) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Under ₹500 | ₹250–450 | 2–3% | 1 week; a local shop delivers |
| ₹500–1,000 | ₹600–1,000 | 4–7% | 2–3 weeks for bulk stock |
| ₹1,000–2,500 | ₹1,200–2,500 | 8–17% | 3–4 weeks, including a choice form |
| ₹2,500–5,000 | ₹2,800–5,000 | 19–33% | 3–4 weeks |
| Signed note to each person | Your time | 0% | 49.4% of Raksha Bandhan 2026 SubhSandesh pages were made on the day (n = 89) |

The takeaway: the first four rows cost money and calendar time, while the note costs neither, and the last row's figure shows how late people tend to leave the personal part.

## Diwali gift ideas for clients: why the employee numbers do not carry over

Both numbers in this post, the ₹15,000 perquisite line and the ₹50,000 GST carve-out, are about an employer giving to an employee. A client is neither, so a client hamper sits under different rules for the giver and the receiver.

Treat client gifts as their own line in the budget, with their own approval and invoice. The cheapest useful step is to ask your CA one question before you place the order: how will this be booked, and does the client's own policy let them accept it?

## Where SubhSandesh fits for an office Diwali, and where it does not

SubhSandesh is not a corporate gifting service, and its own numbers say so. Festival and wedding pages are 144 of 3,894 pages built on it, 3.7%, measured 2026-09-09; the other 96.3% are romantic and everyday pages, and each page is built for one recipient.

Where it does fit is one person, after work. Its Diwali page lets you light a diya at their door with a tag, a row of wish diyas, a rangoli with initials and sky lanterns holding up to six photos, with modes for love, family or a friend, and takes about five minutes. If one colleague has become a close friend, or you want to thank your own family for covering the house while you ran the office party, make them a [Diwali card they light diya by diya](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) and send the private link.

For a teammate's birthday or wedding later in the year, the [full set of SubhSandesh templates](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) covers other occasions. It still sends one page to one person, so it will not replace an HR card for a hundred people.

## When a Diwali gift for employees is the wrong move

A gift does not repair late pay. If salaries or a promised bonus are delayed, a ₹1,000 hamper reads as a substitute, and the experiments above measured gifts on top of a fair wage, not instead of one.

Watch who is on the list. Staff who do not celebrate Diwali may prefer the word "festive season" on the card, and contract staff hired through an agency may not be your employees for the ₹15,000 rule, so ask your CA how their gifts are treated. If the year's total for anyone is close to ₹15,000, skip the Diwali gift and give the note.

- [Perquisites (Income-tax Rules, 1962)](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/w/perquisites), Income Tax Department; no publication date shown.
